clue.text: Reserving energy, switch positions with unique individual

indicators.note: a thing reserving something keeps it held within, so the switch settings enclose the energy symbol

parts.note: a switch has two positions, on and off
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A tip for swapping roles with someone unusual while saving power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch positions' reads like an instruction to swap places, but it is the two settings of a light switch, which 'Reserving' wraps round the energy symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-off is a person or thing of which there is only a single example, quite unlike any other.

clue.text: His home game covered by press

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece covered by another sits beneath it, so the game comes after the press

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: The setter's favourite card game gets written up in the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His' is Rufus (Roger Squires), whose 90th birthday the puzzle marks; he lived in Ironbridge, a Shropshire town named after its famous iron bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironbridge in Shropshire was the setter's place of residence, so it fits as where he lived.

clue.text: See 28
Puzzle set, turns and hands it over

indicators.note: to puzzle is to confuse, so these words are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A crossword is compiled, finished, and passed to the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puzzle' rearranges SET TURNS.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrust something is to give it into another's care, handing responsibility over.

clue.text: Contributor to our duplicitous language

indicators.note: Contributor to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Somebody helps shape the deceitful way we talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contributor to' signals the answer sits inside 'our duplicitous'.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is a tongue spoken chiefly in Pakistan and northern India, an example of a language.

clue.text: Plenty of success in the past, moving round

parts.note: ago means in the past, as in 'long ago'

indicators.note: moving letters shifts them about, so the word round is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a winning streak from years ago while travelling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' looks like part of the scene of travel, but it is the signal to rearrange the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a good run means a sustained spell of things going well, a lengthy stretch of winning.

clue.text: Raise tender for statue

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising a word reads it from the bottom up, so it runs backwards

parts.note: a tender spot is sore

explanation.surface: Someone puts in a bid for a sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' turns SORE upward. 'tender' looks like a bid but means painful.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the famous winged figure atop the fountain in Piccadilly Circus, London, a well-known statue.

clue.text: Giving Gone Girl new review in his extended period at the top

definitions.text: his extended period at the top

indicators.note: to review something is to go over it again, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A critic rewrites a write-up of the thriller Gone Girl during a lengthy career at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'review' is the rearranging signal, not a critique. Rufus was famed as the most prolific crossword setter, with decades of Guardian puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: A long reign is a lengthy spell as top dog, here the setter's many years as a leading compiler.

clue.text: I hear you on the radio

definitions.text: I hear you on the radio

parts.words: I hear you on the radio
parts.note: radio operators acknowledge a message received with a standard word, which also happens to be the setter's first name

explanation.surface: A listener tells a broadcaster they caught the show.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter Rufus is Roger Squires, so the radio acknowledgement doubles as his name.
explanation.definitionFit: In radio procedure this word signals that a message has been received and understood.

clue.text: In navy after misfortune blossomed

indicators.note: the navy letter is placed after the misfortune word

parts.note: a blow is a setback or misfortune

explanation.surface: A sailor's career flowered after a stroke of bad luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Of a flower, blown means fully opened, past bud stage, an old poetic sense.

clue.text: Do cursory alteration to trousers

indicators.note: an alteration changes something's form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tailor is told to make a quick fix to a pair of slacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alteration' rearranges DO CURSORY; it neatly sounds like tailoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Corduroys are pants made of ribbed cotton fabric, a type of trousers.

clue.text: He, as a qualified judge, about to discharge European detained

parts.note: re means about, as in business letters

indicators.note: a thing detained is held inside, so this letter goes within the discharge word

parts.note: to free someone is to discharge them

explanation.surface: A judge is about to release a European prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detained' signals one piece held inside another; 'about to' is not 'soon' but the short word for concerning. Roger Squires was a qualified football referee.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee is the official adjudicating a match, so he served as a sporting judge with qualifications.

clue.text: He was a so-called king

parts.note: William II of England was known by a nickname meaning red-haired, which is also the setter's pseudonym

explanation.surface: A man who only bore the title of monarch in name.
explanation.walkthrough: William II was nicknamed Rufus; 'so-called' means that is what he was called, not that he was a fake king.
explanation.definitionFit: William II's byname was Rufus, the nickname by which this English monarch is known.

clue.text: Rosemary, who sings soprano with broadcast choral groups

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for soprano in music

indicators.note: broadcast means put on air, so the word is as heard rather than spelt

parts.note: choirs are choral groups

explanation.surface: A soprano called Rosemary performs on air alongside choirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns CHOIRS into its sound-alike QUIRES. Rosemary Squires was a British singer; the setter shares the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary Squires was a popular British vocalist, so the singer's surname is wanted.

clue.text: Being in drink here admitted him to the 19 1

definitions.text: Being in drink here admitted him to the 19 1

parts.words: Being in drink here admitted him to the 19 1
parts.note: 'drink' is slang for the sea; a pilot who ditches into it and survives joins the club for such survivors

explanation.surface: A drinking session got him membership of a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in drink' suggests drunkenness, but 'the drink' is the sea. Squires, a Fleet Air Arm pilot, ditched and so joined the Goldfish Club.
explanation.definitionFit: Below the surface of the sea is where the ditched aircrew found themselves before rescue.

clue.text: Endlessly regular, in his place

indicators.note: something endless has lost its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a steady rhythm is a regular one

explanation.surface: A dependable deputy constantly standing in for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Stead means place or role, mostly in the phrase 'in his stead' for a substitute.

clue.text: Devotee starts off filling in easy 9 down

indicators.note: the starts of these words are taken off them, their first letters, with 9 read as the word nine

parts.note: 9 is to be read as the word nine

explanation.surface: A fan begins by filling in an easy clue in the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts off' takes the first letters; 9 must be read as 'nine' to give N.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiend is an enthusiast, as in 'crossword fiend', a keen follower of something.

clue.text: To block noise, sheriff covering those with these?

definitions.note: a phrase of purpose standing for the plural noun: things to block noise

indicators.note: in a down entry the covering piece sits on top, so the sheriff comes first

parts.note: Wyatt Earp was a famous Wild West lawman
lugs, slang for ears

explanation.surface: A sheriff tries to keep out the din by covering his ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'those with these' points to LUGS, slang for ears, the parts that wear the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Earplugs are small stoppers put into the ear canal to shut out sound.

clue.text: What enables one to pinpoint place for doctors

definitions.text: What enables one to pinpoint place
definitions.meaning: the Global Positioning System finds your location by satellite

explanation.definitionFit: The satellite navigation system shares its letters with the plural of the family-medicine abbreviation.

clue.text: Successful ditchers preparing big cold flush

indicators.note: preparing these words works them into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: People who've got rid of something are getting ready for a huge chilly rinse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preparing' rearranges BIG COLD FLUSH. 'ditchers' are airmen who ditched into the sea and lived.
explanation.definitionFit: The Goldfish Club is an association for aircrew who survived coming down into water.

clue.text: In days before, this was him

parts.note: ante is Latin for before, as in antenatal

explanation.surface: Once upon a time, the poet was this very man.
explanation.walkthrough: Before Rufus, Squires set puzzles under the pseudonym Dante, in the Financial Times.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante was another crossword pen name used by the same compiler, so it identifies him too.

clue.text: Keep an eye on certain short curtain

indicators.note: short means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: sure means certain
a veil is a curtain or screen

explanation.surface: Someone peeks round a too-short net curtain to spy on the neighbours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts SURE to SUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To surveil is to keep under watch or surveillance, monitoring closely.

clue.text: Joined by crazy admirer

indicators.note: crazy suggests something disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is wed to an obsessive fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges ADMIRER.
explanation.definitionFit: Married means united in wedlock, so the couple are joined.

clue.text: Possible association of his fans, all Tories?

definitions.meaning: Rufus's puzzles appeared on ..., so a ... for his fans might be named after that day
a right-wing pressure group within the Conservative Party

explanation.definitionFit: The real Monday Club is a Conservative political group; Rufus set the Guardian's Monday puzzle for years.

clue.text: He was a high-flyer who crashed

definitions.text: He was a high-flyer who crashed

parts.words: He was a high-flyer who crashed
parts.note: in Greek myth the son of Daedalus flew too near the sun on wax wings and fell to the sea

explanation.surface: A star performer whose career came to grief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-flyer' suggests a successful person, but it is literal: a mythical flyer who fell.
explanation.definitionFit: In the myth his wings melted when he soared too high, so he plunged into the sea.

clue.text: Refund so, if his work not this amusing?

definitions.text: Refund so, if his work not this amusing?

parts.words: Refund so, if his work not this amusing?
parts.note: a joke demand for money back if the puzzles failed to entertain, the answer being a phrase meaning very amusing

explanation.surface: A solver asks for their money back if his crossword isn't entertaining.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of fun means brimming with enjoyment, the quality expected of Rufus's light-hearted puzzles.

clue.text: Setting not right for celebrity

indicators.note: not here means without, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a frame is a setting, as for a picture

explanation.surface: Puzzle-setting, done without any fuss, brings renown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' drops R from FRAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Fame is the state of being widely known, which is what celebrity means.

clue.text: Clue originally featured in 1 — and never again?

indicators.note: a thing featured in another is set within it

parts.note: the number 1 is the word one

indicators.note: originally means at the very beginning, so take the first letter

explanation.surface: A clue appeared in the first slot, never to be repeated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives C, which 'featured in' puts inside ONE. '1' looks like a cross-reference to 1 Down but is just the number.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Once and never again' describes a single occurrence; the answer means on a single occasion only.

clue.text: Unfortunately, a gap his retirement left?

parts.note: a lack is a gap or absence, here the one left when he stopped setting

explanation.surface: Sadly, his stepping down has left a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Alack is an archaic exclamation of sorrow or regret, like 'alas'.

clue.text: Girl, one on thin ice away from the sides

indicators.note: the sides are the outer letters, which are taken away

parts.note: a skater is someone on ice, literally rather than in the idiom of taking a risk

explanation.surface: A young woman takes a risk, keeping clear of the edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away from the sides' drops the S and R ends of SKATER. 'on thin ice' suggests danger, but is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Kate is a common female forename, a typical crossword example of a girl.

clue.text: He tricked his way into this 1

definitions.text: He tricked his way into this 1

parts.words: He tricked his way into this 1
parts.note: the famous society of conjurors admits members on proof of skill with illusions; 1 Down is club

explanation.walkthrough: 'tricked his way' suggests cheating, but means performing conjuring tricks; Squires was a member of this magicians' society.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magic Circle is the London-based association of professional and amateur magicians.

clue.text: Wearing this one looks like nothing on earth

definitions.text: Wearing this one looks like nothing on earth

parts.words: Wearing this one looks like nothing on earth
parts.note: 'nothing on earth' means bizarre, but literally an astronaut in this outfit is off the planet

explanation.surface: An outfit so outlandish it makes the wearer look ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looks like nothing on earth' is an idiom for looking odd, but read literally it describes an astronaut.
